title: Exact tensor pullback along a flat morphism of ringed topoi
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to the module-sheaf universe, let $A,B$ be sheaves of commutative rings on them, and let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with structural ring map $f^\sharp:f^{-1}B\to A$. Suppose $A$ is flat as an $f^{-1}B$-module sheaf [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] form the tensor pullback $f^*M=A\otimes_{f^{-1}B}f^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $f^*:\operatorname{Mod}(B)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ is additive and exact: it preserves kernels and cokernels and carries every short exact sequence to a short exact sequence. The geometric morphism need not be induced by a functor between the chosen presenting sites.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), second assertion; flatness is definition-flat immediately preceding it.

proof.text: Put $R=f^{-1}B$. The ringed-topos hypothesis gives a geometric morphism, so apply [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact] with source $\mathcal D$, target $\mathcal C$ and ring sheaf $B$. Its transported module functor $I:\operatorname{Mod}(B)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is exact, including kernels and cokernels. It is additive: transported addition is $f^{-1}$ of addition under the finite-product comparison, and a sum of maps is addition after their product with the diagonal. This uses no functor between the presenting sites.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), proof; Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3); Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian) and 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits)

proof.text: By [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], flatness of $A$ as an $R$-module says exactly that $T:N\mapsto N\otimes_R A$ is exact as an endofunctor of $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Let $E(N)=A\otimes_R N$ with $A$ acting on the first factor. The maps $a\otimes n\mapsto n\otimes a$ and $n\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes n$ respect balancing, since $(ra)\otimes n=a\otimes(rn)$, and are mutually inverse on pure tensors. They therefore induce natural inverse sheaf maps for the sheafified tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], identifying the underlying $R$-module of $E(N)$ with $T(N)$. Moreover $E(u+v)(a\otimes n)=a\otimes u(n)+a\otimes v(n)$ and $E(0)=0$, proving additivity.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), proof; Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3); Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian) and 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] to $R$ and $A$ on $\mathcal C$; its sheafification hypothesis holds for the small site in the stipulated universe. Both scalar-forgetting functors preserve kernels and cokernels. Thus the underlying abelian-sheaf maps of the kernel and cokernel comparisons for $E$ are the comparisons for the exact functor $T$, hence isomorphisms. An $A$-linear map invertible on underlying sheaves has $A$-linear inverse: if $u(x)=y$, then $u(ax)=ay$, so $u^{-1}(ay)=a u^{-1}(y)$. Hence the comparison maps are isomorphisms in $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$, and $E$ preserves kernels and cokernels.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), proof; Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3); Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian) and 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits)

proof.text: The given tensor pullback is $f^*=E\circ I$. Its kernel comparison is the composite of the kernel comparisons for $I$ and $E$; the same holds for cokernels, so both are isomorphisms. The composite is additive. For a short exact sequence $0\to M_1\xrightarrow{u}M_2\xrightarrow{v}M_3\to0$, $u$ is a kernel of $v$ and $v$ is a cokernel of $u$ in the abelian module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Their images have these same two properties and form a short exact sequence. This proves every asserted clause.

tool_uses.why: Generic exact inverse-image theorem for arbitrary geometric morphisms and variable commutative ring sheaves; the local groupoid-module argument needs this without a presenting-site functor.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q48-a83ac57df (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item against Stacks 04JC (sites-modules.tex:5540) and 03ER(3). The statement is unchanged and true. Restricting to commutative rings is forced by def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product and matches the only citer. Steps 1-4 are sound. Step 1: the ringed-topos datum is a geometric morphism as in def-trf-geometric-morphism; with the sites swapped, lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact gives the exact transported functor Mod(B)->Mod(f^{-1}B). Step 2: flatness is by definition exactness of N ⊗_R A; the flip A⊗N ≅ N⊗A is elementary. Step 3: scalar forgetting (03DA/03DB node, clause 1) shows the comparisons are isomorphisms, and the inverse of an A-linear bijection is A-linear. Step 4: the comparisons compose, and short exact sequences go to short exact sequences in the abelian categories. Small cases: f=id on a point is ordinary flat base change; A=0 and an empty site are fine; for Z->Z/2, multiplication by 2 becomes the zero map, so flatness is really used. There are no new nodes. The candidates found by rg are all narrower and none is a duplicate: prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact, lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact (needs a site functor), lem-sc-affine-algebra-tensor-pullback-exact. Batch-5 check: I accept lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact. It is the generic first assertion of 04JC, not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality. Its 132-node closure contains only two other trf nodes, both general definitions (def-trf-geometric-morphism, def-trf-abelian-inverse-image-presentation), and no trace-formula, Poincaré or batch-4 node. I accept both tool_uses as generic. No SGA, no repair note, no changes.
